source.title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let (W, ω) be a symplectic manifold with bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity, meaning that every open subset U \subset W with compact closure has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, and let H: W → R be a smooth proper Hamiltonian. If A^P_H denotes the set of regular values a for which the energy level {H = a} carries no periodic orbit of the Hamiltonian flow, how large can A^P_H be? In particular, beyond the fact that almost-existence theorems force A^P_H to have measure zero, what kinds of zero-measure sets can occur as the full set of regular aperiodic values?
accepted.context_brief: Size of the aperiodic energy-value set

evidence.quote: Now we are in a position to state the main question considered in this paper. We call a value a of H aperiodic if the level {H = a} carries no periodic orbits. Let W be a symplectic manifold of bounded capacity and H a smooth proper function on W. How large can the set APH of regular aperiodic values of H be?

accepted.question_text: Fix 2n ≥ 6. Let H_0 on R^{2n} \cong C^n be the quadratic Hamiltonian H_0 = ∑ λ_j |z_j|^2 defining an irrational ellipsoid, where the coefficients λ_j are positive and rationally independent, and let K \subset (0,∞) be a compact set of Lebesgue measure zero. Does there exist a C^∞ Hamiltonian H: R^{2n} → R that is C^0-close to H_0 and isotopic to H_0 through a compactly supported isotopy, such that for every energy value a \in K the level {H = a} has no closed trajectories of the Hamiltonian flow? Equivalently, can one realize an arbitrary compact zero-measure set K as a set of aperiodic regular energy values for such a perturbation of H_0?
accepted.context_brief: Prescribing a compact zero-measure aperiodic set

evidence.quote: An irrational ellipsoid M in the standard symplectic vector space Cn is the unit energy level of the quadratic Hamiltonian H0 = P λj |zj |2, where the eigenvalues λj are positive and rationally independent.

It appears plausible that the function H0 can be modified as in the proof of Theorem 3.1 simultaneously for all energy values from a compact zero measure set K ⊂ (0,∞). The resulting function H will then be smoothly isotopic to H0 and have K as the set of aperiodic values. This leads to the following Conjecture 3.4. For 2n ≥ 6, there exists a C∞-function H : R2n → R, C0-close and isotopic (with a compact support) to H0, such that the Hamiltonian flow of H has no closed trajectories for energy values in the set K.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a proper smooth Hamiltonian system in dimension four with a regular compact energy level that carries no periodic orbit? More specifically, if one starts from G. Kuperberg's C^1 divergence-free vector field on S^3 without periodic orbits, can that vector field be realized as the characteristic flow coming from a C^2 embedding, or even a C^1 embedding, of S^3 into R^4? A positive answer would produce a C^2 Hamiltonian counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

evidence.quote: Neither the method from [Gi2, Gi5] nor from [Her3] apply to four-dimensional manifolds. There are also serious difficulties in adapting Kuperberg's plug, [KuK1], to the symplectic setting. A C1-smooth divergence–free vector field on S3 was found by G. Kuperberg, [KuG]. It is not known whether or not this vector field can be obtained by a C2- (or even C1-) embedding of S3 into R4. Such an embedding would give a C2-smooth "counterexample" to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a compact Riemannian manifold, let σ be a symplectic 2-form on M, and consider the twisted symplectic form ω = ω_0 + π^*σ on T^*M, where ω_0 is the standard symplectic form and π: T^*M → M is the cotangent-bundle projection. For the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy), is it true that some neighborhood of the zero section M \subset T^*M always has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, that almost all energy levels of H carry periodic orbits, and that every sufficiently low energy level carries a contractible periodic orbit?
accepted.context_brief: Twisted geodesic flows near the zero section

evidence.quote: Denote by ω0 the standard symplectic form on T∗M and by π : T∗M → M the natural projection. The form ω = ω0 + π∗σ on T∗M is symplectic (a twisted symplectic structure). The flow of the standard metric Hamiltonian H (the kinetic energy) on (T∗M, ω) describes the motion of a charge on M in the magnetic field σ.

Conjecture 4.2. For every M and any symplectic form σ, a neighborhood of M in T∗M has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity. Moreover, almost all levels of H carry periodic orbits. When σ is symplectic, every low energy level of H has a contractible periodic orbit.

accepted.question_text: Does the cotangent bundle T^*M equipped with a twisted symplectic structure associated with a magnetic field σ have bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity in general? Here bounded capacity means that every relatively compact open subset has finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity. The paper records positive results for certain manifolds and local neighborhoods, but asks whether such boundedness should hold for twisted cotangent bundles in full generality.
accepted.context_brief: Global bounded capacity of twisted cotangent bundles

evidence.quote: Moreover, for some manifolds M, the twisted cotangent bundle has bounded capacity, [GK, Ji, Lu].
Interestingly, there seems to be no sufficient evidence that T∗M has bounded Hofer–Zehnder capacity in general.

accepted.question_text: In the horocycle-flow example, let M be a compact hyperbolic surface of genus at least 2, let σ be its area form, and let H be the kinetic-energy Hamiltonian on T^*M with the twisted symplectic form ω_0 + π^*σ. Example 4.1 shows that the energy level {H = 1} is aperiodic. For energies above that value, do the sublevel domains {H < a} with a > 1 have finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity?
accepted.context_brief: Finite capacity of horocycle-flow sublevel sets

evidence.quote: Example 4.1 (The horocycle flow). Let M be a compact surface of genus g ≥ 2 equipped with a metric of constant negative curvature K = −1. Let σ be the area form on M. Then the Hamiltonian flow on the energy level {H = 1} has no periodic orbits.
For example, it is not known whether in the setting of Example 4.1 the sets {H < a} with a > 1 have finite capacity.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level? In other words, can a Hamiltonian system of magnetic-flow type on a twisted cotangent bundle have at least two distinct regular compact energy levels that carry no periodic orbits?
accepted.context_brief: Multiple aperiodic levels for twisted geodesic flows

evidence.quote: This example has (Hamiltonian) analogues in all even dimensions; see [Gi6, Example 4.2].

Example 4.1 is the only known "naturally arising" example of a Hamiltonian flow with a regular compact aperiodic energy level. Furthermore, this is the only known example of a twisted geodesic flow with an aperiodic energy level. It is not known if there exists a twisted geodesic flow with more than one aperiodic energy level.

accepted.question_text: For the standard symplectic torus T^{2n} with n > 1, is the Hofer–Zehnder capacity finite? Equivalently, does the standard symplectic structure on T^{2n} give a compact symplectic manifold of finite Hofer–Zehnder capacity, even though the paper notes only partial almost-existence results under extra assumptions on the Hamiltonian?
accepted.context_brief: Finite capacity of the standard symplectic torus

evidence.quote: It seems to be unknown whether or not T2n with the standard symplectic structure has finite capacity for n > 1. However, almost existence has been proven for H : T2n → R satisfying some additional conditions; see, e.g., [Ji].

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a proper smooth Hamiltonian on R^{2n} whose set A^P_H of regular aperiodic energy values is dense? The paper argues that the plug-based construction used to create isolated or zero-measure aperiodic levels is unlikely to produce such an example, because away from the constructed aperiodic set the surviving periodic orbits remain non-degenerate and stable, whereas a dense aperiodic set would force every energy level to have only degenerate periodic orbits.

evidence.quote: This method is unlikely to be applicable to the construction of a function H with a dense set APH .
On the other hand, for a system with a dense set APH every energy level must have only degenerate periodic orbits.
